A semantic neighbor does not imply equivalence or safe dual-write behavior.

proposedDomainClasses.D7: Scientific Analysis, Models and Derived Evidence

classification.reason: Common crop names provide controlled cross-domain crop nomenclature; they do not represent an experimental or biological material record.

entries.purpose: Get the Common Crop Names
entries.sourceDescription:
List the common crop names for the crops available in a database server. 

This call is ** required ** for multi-crop systems where data from multiple 
crops may be stored in the same database server. A distinct database server 
is defined by everything in the URL before "/brapi/v2", including host 
name and base path.

This call is recommended for single crop systems to be compatible with 
multi-crop clients. For a single crop system the response should contain 
an array with exactly 1 element. 

The common crop name can be used as a search parameter for Programs, 
Studies, and Germplasm.

entries.purpose: Get the list of implemented Calls
entries.sourceDescription:
Implementation Notes

Having a consistent structure for the path string of each call is very 
important for teams to be able to connect and find errors. Read more on Github.

Here are the rules for the path of each call that should be returned

Every word in the call path should match the documentation exactly, both in 
spelling and capitalization. Note that path strings are all lower case, but 
path parameters are camel case.

Each path should start relative to \"/\" and therefore should not include \"/\"

No leading or trailing slashes (\"/\") 

Path parameters are wrapped in curly braces (\"{}\"). The name of the path parameter 
should be spelled exactly as it is specified in the documentation.

Examples 

GOOD   "call": "germplasm/{germplasmDbId}/pedigree" 

BAD    "call": "germplasm/{id}/pedigree"

BAD    "call": "germplasm/{germplasmDBid}/pedigree" 

BAD    "call": "brapi/v2/germplasm/{germplasmDbId}/pedigree" 

BAD    "call": "/germplasm/{germplasmDbId}/pedigree/" 

BAD    "call": "germplasm/<germplasmDbId>/pedigree

entries.operationName: Update existing `Calls` with new genotype value or metadata

entries.purpose: Update existing `Calls` with new genotype value or metadata
entries.sourceDescription:
Update existing `Calls` with new genotype value or metadata
Implementation Note -
A `Call` object does not have a DbId of its own. It is defined by the unique combination of `callSetDbId`, `variantDbId`, and `variantSetDbId`. These three fields MUST be present for every `call` update request. This endpoint should not allow these fields to be modified for a given `call`. Modifying these fields in the database is effectively moving a cell to a different location in the genotype matrix. This action is dangerous and can cause data collisions.

entries.purpose: Create new image metadata records
entries.sourceDescription:
Create new image metadata records

Implementation Notes

- This endpoint should be implemented with 'PUT /images/{imageDbId}/imagecontent' for full image upload capability

- ''imageURL'' should be a complete URL describing the location of the image. There is no BrAPI call for retrieving 
the image content, so it could be on a different path, or a different host.

- ''descriptiveOntologyTerm'' can be thought of as Tags for the image. These could be simple descriptive words, or 
ontology references, or full ontology URI's.

- The '/images' calls support a GeoJSON object structure for describing their location. The BrAPI spec for GeoJSON 
only supports two of the possible geometries; Points and Polygons.

- With most images, the Point geometry should be used, and it should indicate the longitude and latitude of the camera.

- For top down images (ie from drones, cranes, etc), the Point geometry may be used to indicate the longitude and 
latitude of the centroid of the image content, and the Polygon geometry may be used to indicate the border of the 
image content.

An example use case is available on the BrAPI Wiki -> https://wiki.brapi.org/index.php/Image_Upload

entries.operationName: Get a list of Observations in a table format

classification.reason: Official Phenotyping module; resource-specific exceptions may require review.

entries.purpose: Get a list of Observations in a table format
entries.sourceDescription:
This service is designed to retrieve a table for observation values as a matrix of Observation Units and Observation Variables.

The table may be represented by JSON, CSV, or TSV. The "Accept" HTTP header is used for the client to request different return formats. By default, if the "Accept" header is not included in the request, the server should return JSON as described below.

The table is REQUIRED to have the following columns

  • observationUnitDbId - Each row is related to one Observation Unit
  • At least one column with an observationVariableDbId

The table may have any or all of the following OPTIONAL columns. Included columns are decided by the server developer

  • observationUnitName
  • studyDbId
  • studyName
  • germplasmDbId
  • germplasmName
  • positionCoordinateX
  • positionCoordinateY
  • year

The table also may have any number of Observation Unit Hierarchy Level columns. For example:

  • field
  • plot
  • sub-plot
  • plant
  • pot
  • block
  • entry
  • rep

The JSON representation provides a pair of extra arrays for defining the headers of the table. The first array "headerRow" will always contain "observationUnitDbId" and any or all of the OPTIONAL column header names. The second array "observationVariables" contains the names and DbIds for the Observation Variables represented in the table. By appending the two arrays, you can construct the complete header row of the table.

For CSV and TSV representations of the table, an extra header row is needed to describe both the Observation Variable DbId and the Observation Variable Name for each data column. See the example responses below

entries.operationName: Get a list of Observations in a table format

classification.reason: Official Phenotyping module; resource-specific exceptions may require review.

entries.purpose: Get a list of Observations in a table format
entries.sourceDescription:
This service is designed to retrieve a table of time dependant observation values as a matrix of Observation Units and Observation Variables. This is also sometimes called a Time Series. This service takes the "Sparse Table" approach for representing this time dependant data.

The table may be represented by JSON, CSV, or TSV. The "Accept" HTTP header is used for the client to request different return formats. By default, if the "Accept" header is not included in the request, the server should return JSON as described below.

The table is REQUIRED to have the following columns

  • observationUnitDbId - Each row is related to one Observation Unit
  • observationTimeStamp - Each row is has a time stamp for when the observation was taken
  • At least one column with an observationVariableDbId

The table may have any or all of the following OPTIONAL columns. Included columns are decided by the server developer

  • observationUnitName
  • studyDbId
  • studyName
  • germplasmDbId
  • germplasmName
  • positionCoordinateX
  • positionCoordinateY
  • year

The table also may have any number of Observation Unit Hierarchy Level columns. For example:

  • field
  • plot
  • sub-plot
  • plant
  • pot
  • block
  • entry
  • rep

The JSON representation provides a pair of extra arrays for defining the headers of the table. The first array "headerRow" will always contain "observationUnitDbId" and any or all of the OPTIONAL column header names. The second array "observationVariables" contains the names and DbIds for the Observation Variables represented in the table. By appending the two arrays, you can construct the complete header row of the table.

For CSV and TSV representations of the table, an extra header row is needed to describe both the Observation Variable DbId and the Observation Variable Name for each data column. See the example responses below

entries.purpose: Advertise supported API generations, capabilities, and authentication profiles so clients can negotiate behavior before using optional GenX features.
entries.sourceDescription:
GenX capability negotiation. Served under `/genx/v1/`.

Returns the V2.1 ServerInfo fields plus `brapiVersions`,
`capabilities`, and `authProfiles` so clients negotiate instead of
probing endpoints. V2.1 `GET /serverinfo` under `/brapi/v2/` is
unchanged. A GenX client against a V2.1-only server falls back to the
V2.1 `calls` array.
canBeUsedFor: Discover whether a server advertises GenX and which capabilities/job types it supports.
Choose a documented V2.1 fallback when GenX is not advertised.
mustNotBeUsedFor: Proving that every advertised operation is healthy at this instant.
Calling unadvertised endpoints as feature probes.
Treating the V2.1 ServerInfo payload and ServerInfoV3 as interchangeable.
entries.sideEffects: Read-only; no domain records are created or changed.
entries.idempotency: Read-only; repeated calls have no intended state-changing effects.

entries.purpose: Create a stable BreedingPipeline workstream and append its first immutable revision, or append a new immutable revision to an existing workstream.
entries.sourceDescription: Creates or references a stable workstream identity and registers one immutable pipeline revision. The outer breedingPipelineDbId must exactly match breedingPipelineVersion.breedingPipelineDbId; mismatch is rejected with 400 Bad Request. A new breedingPipelineVersionDbId is required for every additional revision. An append to an existing workstream also supplies expectedCurrentBreedingPipelineVersionDbId as an atomic compare-and-set precondition; explicit null means no currently published revision. Draft revisions record their preparation baseline using basedOnBreedingPipelineVersionDbId and must not claim supersedes/corrects. Published successors use supersedes/corrects; withdrawal revisions use withdraws. Both identify the exact current published revision through revisionRelationship.
canBeUsedFor: Register a stable workstream identity with a new immutable breedingPipelineVersionDbId.
Retry an identical revision safely using the same breedingPipelineVersionDbId.
Append a new version only when expectedCurrentBreedingPipelineVersionDbId matches the current published pointer.
mustNotBeUsedFor: Mutating a published revision; substantive corrections require a new version identity.
Assuming a record is a BrAPI data resource.
Asserting that the catalogue is validated or endorsed.
Bypassing a stale or omitted expected-current precondition when appending to an existing workstream.
entries.sideEffects: Creates a stable workstream identity when unknown and appends one immutable revision. A published or withdrawn revision conditionally advances or clears the current published-version pointer using an atomic expected-current comparison.
entries.idempotency: Replay is keyed by breedingPipelineVersionDbId and the immutable revision payload is compared using JCS (RFC 8785). An identical same-version replay is evaluated before the expected-current precondition and replays even when that precondition is now stale. The same version ID with a different payload is rejected with 409. A new version under an existing pipeline requires expectedCurrentBreedingPipelineVersionDbId (explicit null when no published version exists); the server atomically compares it with the current pointer before append. A stale or omitted precondition is rejected with 409 and no state change.
notes: Published BreedingPipeline revisions are immutable. A new revision requires a new breedingPipelineVersionDbId; the stable breedingPipelineDbId continues to identify the workstream. Pipeline stage occupancy belongs to cohort/material execution under an exact scheme version, not to the pipeline.

D-BP-14 ratifies Option A (optimistic compare-and-set) as the candidate current-pointer concurrency model. It does not promote RFC-154 to normative status; concurrent service behavior and remaining authorization, authority, and measurement gates are outstanding.

Lifecycle relationships are state-specific: drafts use basedOnBreedingPipelineVersionDbId and omit revisionRelationship; published successors use supersedes/corrects; withdrawal revisions use withdraws.

notes: BrAPI v2.1 source YAMLs do not define operationId in the inspected operations; operationIdInSource remains null and recommendedOperationId is an advisory BrAPI-GenX suggestion, not an edit to frozen V2.1 contracts.

BrAPI-GenX D1-D7 mapping for legacy V2.1 operations is a proposed crosswalk inferred from official modules and route semantics, not an endorsed BrAPI reclassification; reviewStatus remains needs-neighbor-review.

bijmantraInventorySnapshot.reconciliation: The 1,921 legacy Python rows include one WS (WebSocket) route, leaving 1,920 HTTP route declarations. The three surface row counts sum to 2,239 HTTP/contract/specification operations plus the single WS row = 2,240 inventory rows.
notes: Source declarations and OpenAPI contracts do not prove runtime mounting or reachability.
A relative path match does not prove wire compatibility, authorization compatibility, data ownership, or safe mirroring.
Rust boundary routes generally include capability-specific base paths and are cross-referenced as semantic candidates, not route equivalences.
A null primaryDomain is allowed only for a shared cross-cutting resource and must carry at least one explicit crossCuttingCapability.
Cross-cutting facets describe contract behavior, not scientific equivalence or implementation support.
Legacy v2.1 module grouping remains authoritative and unchanged; D1-D7 is a BrAPI-GenX crosswalk that requires scientific review.

confidenceScale.low: Route/module-derived mapping that needs substantial scientific review
confidenceScale.medium: Plausible mapping from source semantics; still awaiting independent domain review
confidenceScale.high: Reviewed and approved mapping with recorded rationale; none is asserted high until that review occurs

semanticRelationships.title: Server capability discovery
semanticRelationships.relationship: Same broad discovery purpose across API generations; V2.1 ServerInfo and GenX ServerInfoV3 are not interchangeable payload contracts.
doNotAssume: A V2.1 response contains GenX capability fields.
The existence of the same relative route proves the same response schema.

semanticRelationships.title: Seed-lot transactions versus ledger entries
semanticRelationships.relationship: Both can describe real-world material movement, but identity, quantity representation, ordering, atomicity and replay guarantees differ. No one-to-one event mapping or safe mirroring contract is established.
doNotAssume: Do not silently mirror one movement into both records.
Do not double-count both streams as independent movements.
Do not treat the GenX ledger as a drop-in replacement for V2.1 SeedLotTransaction.

semanticRelationships.title: V2.1 search-results lifecycle versus GenX Jobs
semanticRelationships.relationship: Jobs is a general asynchronous-work lifecycle; V2.1 search operations use a search-specific lifecycle. A server may implement search through Jobs only when that behavior is explicitly advertised.
doNotAssume: Do not translate a V2.1 search-result identifier to a jobDbId.
Do not assume a V2.1 search endpoint is replaced by Jobs.
Do not assume a job type exists unless advertised.

semanticRelationships.title: Scientific observations versus telemetry samples
semanticRelationships.relationship: V2.1 observations are linked to observation variables and observation units/studies; GenX telemetry is a device/sensor time series. Mapping requires explicit variable, unit, time, quality, study/unit and provenance rules.
doNotAssume: Do not convert telemetry to Observation records by field-name similarity.
Do not infer an observation unit, study or observation variable from a device/sensor identifier.

semanticRelationships.title: Genotyping records versus VariantMatrix references
semanticRelationships.relationship: VariantMatrix identifies and verifies an external matrix; it does not replace VariantSet, Variant, CallSet or Calls records and does not provide matrix bytes.
doNotAssume: Do not expect matrix bytes from a VariantMatrix metadata endpoint.
Do not treat VariantMatrix as a synonym for VariantSet or Calls.
Do not assume GenX defines a new slicing or external-byte authorization protocol.

semanticRelationships.title: File references versus FAIR packages
semanticRelationships.relationship: A FAIRPackage adds citation, licensing, access-rights and embargo metadata around payload references. It is not a payload-byte endpoint. The V2.1 metadata.datafiles schema is an adjacent schema-level concept.
brapiV21SchemaReferences: metadata.datafiles and external file retrieval links
doNotAssume: Do not assume FAIRPackage uploads or stores payload bytes.
Do not infer persistent-identifier minting or restricted-access approval workflows from registration.

semanticRelationships.title: Observation-variable definitions versus VariableTerm versions
semanticRelationships.relationship: V2.1 ObservationVariable and OntologyTerm contracts are not interchangeable with GenX's namespaced, versioned VariableTerm. Term equivalence and authority mapping need a separate rule.
doNotAssume: Do not treat VariableTerm as a replacement for V2.1 OntologyTerm.
Do not infer term equivalence from labels.
Do not assume full Trait/Method/Scale lifecycle or cross-authority mapping is standardized by RFC-002.

semanticRelationships.title: Model registration versus inference execution
semanticRelationships.relationship: Model registry endpoints manage model metadata and lifecycle. Inference is submitted as a supported Job, not through a synchronous /models/{id}/infer operation.
doNotAssume: Do not infer training or inference from a model registration/read operation.
Do not assume a revoked flag alone defines approval governance.
Do not invent a synchronous inference route.
